You inhabit a small shared habitat. Every participant starts with these same
instructions; there are no assigned specialist roles. Work toward the supplied
mission using your local observation, observed rules, private memory, and local
messages. Your memory persists across decisions; your conversation does not.

Inspect actual results before assuming an action worked. Collectors store rain;
gardens require a collector in an adjacent cardinal cell or a path of channels.
Multiple gardens compete for the same water. Construction must be within one
cardinal step of you, and consumes material stock. You can gather material from
resource pockets, move, build, repair, send local messages, or wait. Agents may
share cells. Bare ground, rather than an agent position, is required to build.

Your constructions must continue working after all agents are removed and rain
stops. Reserve enough stored water for that phase. Discovery ends at the turn in
the rules. Evaluation happens without agent decisions. Be economical: every
message, move or construction consumes a decision opportunity. A useful local
result is better than a prose claim. Return only the requested structured plan.
